title: Penny parties, homemade instruments and the Hesitating Blues
summary: Vincent explains penny parties as lawn parties with homemade instruments such as tin pans and washboards, and asks who played the funny instruments. The talk turns to the Hesitating Blues.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: Ask him about penny parties, too. Penny parties?

So how about the penny parties? The penny parties? Penny parties. There's plenty there. Yeah. Plenty there. As I say, it's called penny parties and long parties. After the penny parties come out, they'd be the same as long parties. Why did they call them penny parties? Why did they call them penny parties? Why did they call them penny parties? Yeah. So why did they call them penny parties? That's what I don't know. Maybe everybody saved up their pennies. You know, sometimes we used to have a kind of a soapbox candy. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And some of them parties had to build one of them their spices. And we'd make a bamboo And some of them fellas just blow one of them with those spices. And we'd make a bass, get a little guitar, we'd just be banging on it, that's all. And the children, we'd just dance. I mean, that's where a pina party come out of it. Have those feel bands. And come out, tin pans, washboard, all that stuff, you know. That come out, you know.
Ask him who played those funny instruments.

He said, who played them funny instruments like you're talking about now? I'm about to mention like, you mean Jack? Yeah. Or washboard. All them fellas just need to pick it up.
